Olivia (Support): Hey team, escalated ticket from Dexter — embeddings endpoint is returning wrong vector size after switching precision profile. Customer says previously embeddings were 1536, now getting 768. :rotating_light:
Olivia (Support): They also see a "DimensionMismatch: expected 1536 got 768" error when batching multiple texts.
Dexter (Customer): @olivia yeah we switched to the recommended int8 quant profile to save cost. All we changed was precision=\"int8\" in the request config and now our similarity search breaks.
Andrew (Eng-ML): Noted. Quantization shouldn't change embedding dimensionality. Two quick possibilities: 1) model fallback/routing picked a smaller model variant (e.g., ada-embedding-768) when int8 not supported on primary variant, 2) response post-processing in client altered shape.
Maria (SRE): Can you paste the raw API call (no creds) and the response headers so we can check model-id returned by the runtime?
Dexter (Customer): Here is the call we made:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood-embedding-v2",
  "precision": "int8",
  "inputs": ["doc1","doc2","doc3"],
  "batch_size": 8
}
```
And the error (from our SDK):
```
Error: DimensionMismatch: expected 1536 got 768
    at EmbeddingClient._validate (sdk/embeddings.js:112)
    at processBatch (sdk/embeddings.js:78)
```
Olivia (Support): Thanks. Two probes: 1) did you see any `x-redwood-model` or `x-redwood-variant` header in the response? 2) can you try a single input (no batching) with precision=int8 and paste the top-level JSON?
Dexter (Customer): Single input returns a vector length 768 too. No special headers in our capture (we'll re-check).
Andrew (Eng-ML): Ok that rules out client-side batching bug. Hypothesis: quantization profile mapping logic in routing selected `redwood-embedding-small-int8` fallback which is 768-dim. Customer likely specified a precision profile not available for the large model on the allocated pool, so the router picked a compatible smaller variant.
Maria (SRE): I'll pull routing logs for Dexter's org id. Olivia, can you send me the request id?
Olivia (Support): Request id coming from customer: `req_0a7f3b9c`
SupportBot: Incident link created -> https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0315-emb-dim
Maria (SRE): Got it. I see the routing decision: model requested `redwood-embedding-v2` with `precision=int8`. Cluster did not have int8 kernels for v2 so policy `fallback_to_compatible_variant` selected `redwood-embedding-v2-small-int8` variant (dim=768).
Maria (SRE): Logs: `ROUTER DECISION: fallback_to_variant redwood-embedding-v2-small-int8 reason=quant_profile_unavailable`.
Andrew (Eng-ML): That matches. The real bug is ambiguous UX: customers expect precision to only change numeric type, not model variant. We need clearer telemetry and an explicit `variant_selected` header returned.
Olivia (Support): For the customer, recommended workaround? Force `model_version` or pin `variant`?
Andrew (Eng-ML): Short-term: ask them to set force_variant=\"redwood-embedding-v2\" or remove precision override. Also can set allow_fallback=false in request to get a 409 instead of silent downgrade — we'll expose that flag in docs.
Dexter (Customer): Forcing variant worked, we got 1536 vectors again, but throughput dropped and latency increased (expected). Is there a safe quantization path to keep dims=1536 while using int8?
Andrew (Eng-ML): Two notes: 1) Quantization should not change dimension; int8 for the v2 large model is only available on specific hardware/kernel combos (we don't have it on your assigned pool). 2) We have a quant profile `fp16->mixed-int8` that keeps the large weights and uses per-channel quantization — but only available as a per-customer compile in Dedicated.
Maria (SRE): Also customer observed batching error earlier — that's because their client SDK validates vector length against expected model dims. When router silently downgraded variant, the SDK still held expected_dim=1536, so batch validation failed.
Olivia (Support): Action items: 1) ask customer to set allow_fallback=false and/or pin variant (workaround), 2) offer to route them to a pool that has int8 kernels (if they want cost saving), 3) file product bug for clearer response headers and doc update.
Andrew (Eng-ML): I'll open PR to 1) add `x-redwood-selected-variant` header, 2) add `allow_fallback` boolean in the API, and 3) return `400` with a clear message if dims mismatch with allow_fallback=false.
Olivia (Support): I'll send Dexter a step-by-step repro and temporary config: set \"allow_fallback\": false, \"model\": \"redwood-embedding-v2\", \"precision\": \"int8\" and expect a 409 or 422 with explanation.
Dexter (Customer): Thanks, that will unblock us. Also please confirm whether fp16 -> int8 will degrade semantic quality for our corpus — we saw a tiny drop in recall.
Andrew (Eng-ML): FP16->int8 can impact nearest-neighbor quality slightly depending on quant scheme and dataset. We should run accuracy eval vs their sample prompts. Offer: ask them for a small eval set and we'll run 1k-pair recall test on both fp16 and int8 on the same model.
Maria (SRE): Filed incident note and escalated to runtime team.
Olivia (Support): I'll send the workaround + offer to run eval. Marking as escalated internally until PRs land. :thumbsup:
